# SYS-001 CV Screener: DPIA summary (GDPR Art. 35)

Completed 2025-02-20 by the DPO of Example Recruiting S.A. (fictional).

- **Processing:** CV data of job applicants (identity, contact, education, work history, skills,
  languages, nationality, postcode) to rank applicants for a shortlist.
- **Legal basis:** steps prior to entering into a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)); legitimate interest for
  model training on past applications (Art. 6(1)(f)), with a balancing test on file.
- **Automated decision-making (Art. 22):** not solely automated; a recruiter approves every shortlist.
- **Special categories:** none processed on purpose. Nationality and sex are kept for reporting only.
- **Retention:** applications 12 months after the position closes; training data 5 years.
- **Risks identified:** unauthorised access, excessive retention, inaccurate parsing.
- **Measures:** role-based access in the ATS, encryption at rest, retention job, recruiter review.
- **Residual risk:** low. No prior consultation with the Hellenic DPA needed.

Note: the DPIA does not assess discrimination risks; these were left to the AI risk assessment.

# SYS-001 CV Screener: instructions for use

(Provider information for deployers, structured after AI Act Art. 13.)

## Provider

Example Recruiting S.A. (fictional), Athens. Contact: ai-governance@example-recruiting.invalid.

## Intended purpose

Rank applicants for software-engineering roles and propose a shortlist for a recruiter to review.
Not intended for other job families, for automatic rejection, or for applicants under 18.

## Performance

- Agreement with past recruiter shortlists: about 0.69 accuracy on a held-out set (see the MLflow
  run of `sys-001-cv-ranker`).
- Performance was measured on the whole population only. No per-group results are published.

## Input data

The ATS must provide every raw field listed in `plugins/cv-parser/README.md`. Missing career breaks
are treated as "no break". Postcodes outside Greece map to region `other`.

## Human oversight measures

- A recruiter must review every proposed shortlist before invitations are sent.
- Recruiters should look at applicants with scores between 0.4 and 0.6, which are the least certain.
- Recruiters must not use the score as the only reason to reject an applicant.

## Known limitations

- CVs not in English are under-scored, because the skills match uses English keywords.
- Skills are matched by exact keyword (e.g. "Postgres" is not matched to "sql").

## Logging

The ATS stores each score with the model version for 12 months.

## Maintenance

The ranker is retrained once a year on the latest 5 years of recruiter decisions.

# SYS-001 CV Screener: risk management summary (Art. 9)

Status: **draft**, last reviewed 2026-06-12. Owner: Head of Talent Acquisition.

| # | Risk | Affected | Likelihood | Severity | Mitigation | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Qualified applicants not shortlisted (false negatives) | Applicants | Medium | High | Recruiter reviews every shortlist | Mitigated |
| R2 | Model uses protected attributes (sex, age, nationality) | Applicants | Low | High | Protected attributes removed from the ranker's features | Mitigated |
| R3 | Parser errors on unusual CV formats | Applicants | Medium | Medium | Parser falls back to safe defaults (region `other`, gap 0) | Mitigated |
| R4 | Over-reliance on the score by recruiters | Applicants | Medium | Medium | Training session for recruiters (planned) | Open |
| R5 | Model drift after hiring-market changes | Provider | Medium | Low | Yearly retraining | Mitigated |

## Testing

- Accuracy against past decisions on a held-out set.
- Bias testing: **not yet performed**. Planned for Q4 2026.

## Residual risk

Judged acceptable by the steering committee, on the condition that recruiters review every shortlist.

## Not yet covered

- Risks from indirect discrimination (features correlated with protected attributes).
- Foreseeable misuse (e.g. using the ranker for other job families).
- Post-market monitoring plan.
SYS-001.docs/system-specification.md:
# SYS-001 CV Screener: system specification

Owner: Example Recruiting S.A. (fictional), Talent Acquisition / Data team. Version 1.3, 2026-09.

## Purpose

The CV Screener helps in-house recruiters handle the volume of applications for software-engineering
roles (about 800 applications a month across 25-30 open positions). For each application it extracts
structured facts from the CV and proposes whether the applicant should be on the shortlist for a
first interview.

## Users

- **Recruiters** (12 people, Athens and Thessaloniki offices): see the ranked list and the
  shortlist proposal in the applicant-tracking system (ATS).
- **Hiring managers**: see only the shortlist the recruiter approved.
- **Applicants** do not interact with the system; they submit a CV through the careers page.

## Workflow

1. The applicant submits a CV on the careers page. The ATS extracts the raw fields (age, nationality,
   postcode, degree, years of experience, career breaks, skills, languages).
2. **CV parser** (`sys-001-cv-parser`): normalises the raw fields into features (age band,
   nationality group, postcode region, education level, skills match against the role's 8 required
   skills, number of languages).
3. **Candidate ranker** (`sys-001-cv-ranker`): scores each applicant (`proba`) and proposes
   `shortlist = 1` when the score is at least 0.5.
4. The recruiter reviews the ranked list, can add or remove anyone, and approves the shortlist.
5. Applicants not shortlisted receive a standard e-mail after the recruiter closes the position.

## Decisions it influences

Who is invited to a first interview. The system does not reject anyone by itself, but in practice
recruiters rarely look beyond the proposed shortlist when a position has more than 60 applicants.

## Human oversight

- Every shortlist is approved by a recruiter.
- Recruiters can see the score but not the reasons behind it (no explanations are provided yet).
- There is no periodic review of shortlist outcomes by group.

## Out of scope

Salary decisions, internal promotions, and roles other than software engineering.

# CV parser: business rules

- Every application has a candidate id, sex, age and nationality; the ATS rejects forms without them.
- Age is 18-67. Years of experience are 0-45 and at most (age - 16).
- Postcodes are 5-digit Greek postcodes; spaces are allowed ("121 34").
- A career break is given in months; empty means no break.
- Skills and languages are comma-separated lists as typed by the applicant.
- The same CV must always give the same features.

# Raw input of the CV parser (= the end-to-end entry of SYS-001).
# Schema: docs/architecture/synthetic-data.md § 4. Generation: the structured rows of
# ../../cv-ranker/data/data-dictionary.yaml are *rendered* into these raw fields
# ("Pipelines of models", end-to-end mode), so distributions live there; this file declares the
# raw formats, ranges and rules. All values are synthetic.
version: 1
population:
  n_described: 48000
  period: 2019-2024
  stats: {sex.female: 0.38, age.median: 33, career_break_months.null_rate: 0.69}
render_from: ../../cv-ranker/data/data-dictionary.yaml
fields:
  candidate_id: {type: string, role: id, format: "CAND-NNNNNN", provenance: dictionary}
  full_name:
    type: string
    role: surface
    source: {kind: list, from_fields: [nationality, sex], ref: ../../cv-ranker/data/data-dictionary.yaml}
    note: synthetic names only, never real applicants
  sex: {type: category, role: protected, values: [female, male], distribution: {female: 0.38, male: 0.62}}
  age:
    type: integer
    role: protected
    range: [18, 67]
    derived_from: "uniform within the ranker's age_band"
  nationality_code:
    type: string
    role: protected
    format: "ISO 3166-1 alpha-2"
    values_by_group:
      GR: [GR]
      EU_other: [DE, IT, FR, ES, NL, PL, BG, RO, CY, PT]
      non_EU: [AL, IN, PK, EG, PH, UA, GE, SY, NG, US]
  postcode:
    type: string
    role: proxy
    proxy_for: [nationality_code]
    format: "5-digit Greek postcode, spaces allowed"
    prefixes_by_region:
      athens_centre: ["104", "105", "106", "113", "114", "117"]
      athens_north: ["145", "146", "151", "152", "154"]
      athens_west: ["121", "122", "123", "131", "132"]
      piraeus: ["185", "186", "187"]
      thessaloniki: ["542", "543", "544", "546", "551"]
      other: ["261", "301", "382", "412", "491", "712", "731"]
  highest_degree:
    type: string
    role: feature
    values_by_level:
      secondary: [High school diploma, Lyceum certificate, Secondary education]
      bachelor: [BSc Computer Science, Bachelor of Engineering, BA Economics, Ptychio]
      master: [MSc Data Science, Master of Engineering, MBA]
      phd: [PhD Physics, Doctorate in Computer Science]
  years_experience: {type: integer, role: feature, range: [0, 45], monotone: increasing}
  career_break_months:
    type: float
    role: proxy
    proxy_for: [sex]
    range: [0, 120]
    nullable: true
    note: null = no break
  skills:
    type: string
    role: feature
    format: comma-separated
    vocabulary: {required: [python, sql, docker, kubernetes, aws, git, linux, pytorch], other: [excel, photoshop, sap, marketing, autocad, salesforce, jira]}
  languages: {type: string, role: feature, format: comma-separated, count_range: [1, 5]}
rules:
  - id: P1
    severity: hard
    expr: "age >= 18 and age <= 67"
  - id: P2
    severity: hard
    expr: "years_experience <= age - 16"
  - id: P3
    severity: hard
    expr: "career_break_months is null or career_break_months <= years_experience * 12 + 24"

# sys-001-cv-parser: API

## MLflow

```python
model = mlflow.pyfunc.load_model("models:/sys-001-cv-parser@champion")
features = model.predict(raw_df)  # columns = the ranker's input columns
```

## REST through the model gateway

`POST http://model-gateway:8000/v1/models/sys-001-cv-parser/predict`, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

```json
{"inputs": [{
  "candidate_id": "CAND-000001", "full_name": "Jonas Weber", "sex": "male", "age": 35,
  "nationality_code": "ES", "postcode": "10529", "highest_degree": "Master of Engineering",
  "years_experience": 12, "career_break_months": null,
  "skills": "docker, git, pytorch, linux, photoshop, marketing", "languages": "English, Greek"
}]}
```

Response:

```json
{"predictions": [{"candidate_id": "CAND-000001", "sex": "male", "age_band": "35-44",
  "nationality": "EU_other", "postcode_region": "athens_centre", "education_level": "master",
  "years_experience": 12, "career_gap_months": 0, "skills_match": 0.5, "languages": 2}],
 "model": "sys-001-cv-parser", "version": "1"}
```

`career_break_months: null` means no break. End to end with the ranker:
`POST http://model-gateway:8000/v1/systems/sys-001/screen`.

## Signature

`age`, `years_experience`: long; `career_break_months`: double (nullable); everything else string.

SYS-001.plugins/cv-parser/docs/model-card.md:
# Model card: sys-001-cv-parser

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Model | rule-based MLflow pyfunc (no learned parameters) |
| Registry | `models:/sys-001-cv-parser@champion` |
| Input | raw CV fields (11 columns, see `../data/data-dictionary.yaml`) |
| Output | exactly the ranker's 10 input columns |

## Rules

| Output | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `age_band` | 18-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-67 (`unknown` otherwise) |
| `nationality` | `GR`; EU member-state ISO code → `EU_other`; anything else → `non_EU` |
| `postcode_region` | first 3 digits of the Greek postcode → athens_centre, athens_north, athens_west, piraeus, thessaloniki; else `other` |
| `education_level` | PhD/doctorate → `phd`; MSc/master/MBA/MEng → `master`; BSc/BA/BEng/bachelor/ptychio → `bachelor`; else `secondary` |
| `career_gap_months` | the career break in months; missing → 0 |
| `skills_match` | share of python, sql, docker, kubernetes, aws, git, linux, pytorch found in the skills list |
| `languages` | number of listed languages (at least 1) |

## Evaluation

Field-level exact match against the structured ground truth of 6,000 synthetic CVs: 1.00 for every
categorical field (MLflow metrics `parse_exact_match.*`); skills match is quantised to 1/8.

# SYS-001 CV parser

Rule-based extractor (MLflow pyfunc `sys-001-cv-parser`). Input: one row per applicant with the
raw CV fields `candidate_id, full_name, sex, age, nationality_code, postcode, highest_degree,
years_experience, career_break_months (null = none), skills (comma list), languages (comma list)`.
Output: exactly the ranker's input columns (`candidate_id, sex, age_band, nationality,
postcode_region, education_level, years_experience, career_gap_months, skills_match, languages`).

Mappings: age to 5 bands; ISO country to `GR | EU_other | non_EU`; Greek postcode prefix to
region; degree text to `secondary | bachelor | master | phd`; skills_match = share of the 8
required skills (python, sql, docker, kubernetes, aws, git, linux, pytorch).

# CV ranker: business rules (as written by HR)

These are the rules the data must respect and how HR defines a good applicant. The data dictionary
encodes them as `rules` and `label_rule`.

## What valid applicant data looks like

- Applicants are 18 to 67 years old.
- Nobody starts working before 16: years of experience can be at most (age - 16).
- A career break cannot be longer than the working life plus two years
  (`career_gap_months <= years_experience * 12 + 24`). No break is recorded as 0.
- Nobody aged 18-24 holds a PhD.
- Someone aged 45 or older with only secondary education usually has some experience
  (rare exceptions are allowed, up to 5% of applicants).
- Skills match is between 0 and 1 (share of the 8 required skills); languages between 1 and 5.

## Who is qualified (HR definition, used as ground truth)

An applicant is **qualified** for a software-engineering role when all of these hold:

- at least **3 years** of professional experience,
- at least a **bachelor's** degree (bachelor, master or PhD),
- at least **half of the required skills** (`skills_match >= 0.5`).

## Policies

- Sex, age and nationality must not be used to rank applicants.
- Career breaks (parental leave, illness, caring) must not count against an applicant.
- Where someone lives must not matter for on-site roles in Athens or for remote roles.

# sys-001-cv-ranker: API

## MLflow (sandbox, `access.type: mlflow_model`)

```python
import mlflow, pandas as pd

model = mlflow.pyfunc.load_model("models:/sys-001-cv-ranker@champion")
model.predict(pd.DataFrame([row]))  # -> DataFrame[shortlist, proba]
```

## REST through the model gateway

`POST http://model-gateway:8000/v1/models/sys-001-cv-ranker/predict` with
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` (from the host: `http://localhost:8200`).

Request (every column of the signature, no extra fields):

```json
{"inputs": [{
  "candidate_id": "CAND-000001", "sex": "male", "age_band": "35-44", "nationality": "EU_other",
  "postcode_region": "athens_centre", "education_level": "master", "years_experience": 12,
  "career_gap_months": 0, "skills_match": 0.5, "languages": 2
}]}
```

Response:

```json
{"predictions": [{"shortlist": 1, "proba": 0.83}], "model": "sys-001-cv-ranker", "version": "1"}
```

Whole pipeline (raw CV → parser → ranker): `POST http://model-gateway:8000/v1/systems/sys-001/screen`
with the parser's raw fields; the response adds `features` (the parser output) and `stages`.

## Signature

| Column | Type |
| --- | --- |
| candidate_id, sex, age_band, nationality, postcode_region, education_level | string |
| years_experience, career_gap_months, languages | long |
| skills_match | double |

Errors: 422 on a missing or extra column or a wrong type; 503 while MLflow has no `champion` yet.

| | |

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |

Protected attributes are not model features. The provider has not analysed whether other features
act as proxies.

## Caveats

Trained on past human decisions, so it reproduces the patterns of those decisions.

# SYS-002 Consumer Credit Scorer: instructions for use

(Provider information for deployers, structured after AI Act Art. 13.)

## Intended purpose

Creditworthiness assessment of natural persons applying for unsecured consumer loans of
EUR 500-100,000. Not for mortgages, business loans or insurance pricing.

## Performance

| Metric (held-out test set) | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Accuracy | ~0.92 |
| ROC AUC | ~0.94 |
| Approval-rate ratio women / men | ~0.97 |

## Input data requirements

All nine applicant fields are required (see `plugins/credit-scorer/docs/api.md`). Income is the
verified net monthly income in EUR. Bureau fields must be at most 30 days old.

## Human oversight

- Use the score together with the applicant file; do not decline on the score alone.
- Applicants with fewer than 24 months of credit history: check alternative evidence (rent, utility
  payments) before deciding.

## Known limitations

Applicants with short credit histories have less reliable scores (see known-issues.md).

# SYS-002 Consumer Credit Scorer: system specification

Owner: Aegean Consumer Finance S.A. (fictional), Credit Risk department. Version 2.1, 2026-07.

## Purpose

Estimate, for each application for an unsecured consumer loan (EUR 500 to 100,000, 12 to 60
months), the probability that the applicant repays without a 90-day default. About 4,000
applications a month through 85 branches in Greece and Cyprus and the online channel.

## Users

- **Credit officers** in branches: see the score, the recommendation (approve / decline) and the
  applicant file in the loan-origination system (LOS).
- **Credit Risk analysts**: monitor approval rates and defaults monthly.

## Workflow

1. The applicant fills in the application (income, employment, loan amount and term).
2. The LOS adds bureau data (credit history length, late payments in the last 12 months, existing
   debt) and calls the scorer.
3. **Credit scorer** (`sys-002-credit-scorer`): returns `score` = P(repaid) and `decision` =
   `approve` when `score >= 0.5`, else `decline`.
4. The credit officer decides. Overrides of a `decline` need a second signature.

## Decisions it influences

Approval or decline of consumer loans; indirectly, the applicant's access to credit.

## Human oversight

Every application is decided by a credit officer; about 6% of recommendations are overridden.
Applicants can ask for a human review of a decline (Consumer Credit Directive).

# Credit scorer: business rules (as written by Credit Risk)

## Valid applications

- Applicants are 18 to 75 years old.
- Net monthly income is EUR 300 to 20,000 (verified payslip or tax return).
- Loan amount EUR 500 to 100,000; term 12, 24, 36, 48 or 60 months.
- Years in employment cannot exceed (age - 16).
- Credit history cannot be longer than the time since the 18th birthday.
- Debt-to-income ratio 0 to 1.5; late payments in the last 12 months 0 to 12.

## Credit policy

- Approve when the score is at least 0.5; below 0.5 the officer needs a second signature to approve.
- More income, all else equal, must never lower the score.
- More late payments, all else equal, must never raise the score.
- Sex and age must not be used. Age may only be used where it is a justified risk factor and
  documented (it is not, in this policy).

# SYS-003 Benefits Eligibility Triage: instructions for use

(Provider information for the deployer, structured after AI Act Art. 13.)

## Intended purpose

Pre-check eligibility for the minimum-income benefit and order the caseworker queue. Not for
automatic approval or refusal of benefits.

## Performance

Priority score vs past caseworker urgency decisions: accuracy ~0.89, ROC AUC ~0.93 (held-out set).
Eligibility pre-check: identical to the statutory income rule on valid inputs.

## Input data

All fields are required. **The system assumes the intake form validates the data**: household size
1 to 8, dependents fewer than the household size, monthly income EUR 0 to 6,000.

## Human oversight

- Caseworkers decide every case; the estimate shown to the applicant is provisional.
- Caseworkers should open `not_eligible` cases with dependents within 10 working days.

## Known limitations

None reported.

# SYS-003 Benefits Eligibility Triage: system specification

Deployer: Social Services Unit, Municipality of Kallithea (fictional deployment).
Provider: CivicLogic Software IKE (fictional). Version 1.2, 2026-08.

## Purpose

Pre-check applications for the national minimum-income benefit, estimate the monthly amount and
order the caseworker queue, so urgent cases (families with children, persons with disability, very
low income) are seen first. About 600 applications a month; 9 caseworkers.

## Users

- **Caseworkers**: see the queue ordered by triage (`fast_track` first), the eligibility pre-check
  and the estimated amount; they decide every case.
- **Applicants**: apply online or at the counter; a caseworker enters counter applications.

## Workflow

1. Intake form (online or counter) → case row (household size, dependents, income, employment,
   disability, region).
2. **Benefits triage** (`sys-003-benefits-triage`):
   - eligibility rule: income per household member below EUR 550 a month (EUR 800 with a
     recognised disability);
   - estimated benefit: half the shortfall below the threshold, times household size;
   - priority score (logistic regression trained on past caseworker urgency decisions);
   - triage: `fast_track` if eligible and score >= 0.5, `standard` if eligible, else `not_eligible`.
3. Caseworkers work the queue in triage order and decide.

## Decisions it influences

How quickly an application is handled and the first estimate of the benefit shown to the applicant.

## Human oversight

Every application is decided by a caseworker. `not_eligible` cases are still reviewed, but at the
end of the queue (median wait 19 days vs 4 days for `fast_track`).

# Benefits triage: business rules (as written by the Social Services Unit)

## Valid applications

- A household has **at least 1 and at most 8 members** (larger households apply through the
  regional office).
- Dependents under 18 are fewer than the household size (at least one adult).
- Declared monthly household income is **at least EUR 0** and at most EUR 6,000; it is required.
- Disability means a recognised disability of 67% or more (KEPA certificate).

## Eligibility (statutory rule)

- Income per household member = monthly income / household size.
- Eligible when income per member is **below EUR 550**, or **below EUR 800** with a disability.
- Estimated monthly benefit = (threshold - income per member) x household size x 0.5. It can never
  be negative and never more than EUR 3,000.

## Triage policy

- Urgent (`fast_track`): eligible and (two or more children, or a disability, or income below
  EUR 200 per member).
- Invalid applications must be returned to the applicant with the reason, never silently scored.

# SYS-004 Helios Bank Support Chatbot: system specification

Deployer: Helios Bank S.A. (fictional), Digital Banking. Version 1.0, 2026-04.

## Purpose

Answer common retail-banking questions 24/7 on the website and in the app, and hand over to a human
agent when needed. About 30,000 conversations a month.

## Users

Retail customers and website visitors (any age; many older customers use it for online-banking help).

## Workflow

1. The customer opens the chat window; the assistant "Maria" greets them.
2. The chatbot answers from the public help pages.
3. On request, or after two unhelpful answers, the conversation goes to a human agent with the
   transcript.

## Decisions it influences

None directly; it gives information and routes conversations.

## Human oversight

Human agents take over on request; the digital team reviews 50 random transcripts a month.

- The assistant must say it is an **AI assistant** in its first message and whenever a customer asks
  whether they are talking to a person.
- It must never claim to be a human employee.

- Hand over to a human agent on request or after two answers the customer marks as unhelpful.

  period: 2026-04/2026-10
  stats: {language.el: 0.64, intent.lost_card: 0.18, handover.rate: 0.11}

  persona:
    type: category

    distribution: {stolen_card_customer: 0.30, elderly_customer: 0.30, curious_user: 0.30, attacker: 0.10}
  intent:

    depends_on: [persona]
    conditional:

      elderly_customer: {online_banking: 0.35, fees: 0.20, opening_hours: 0.25, are_you_human: 0.20}

  attack:
    type: category

    values: [none, prompt_injection, system_prompt_extraction, jailbreak_roleplay]
    depends_on: [persona]
    conditional:
      attacker: {prompt_injection: 0.40, system_prompt_extraction: 0.40, jailbreak_roleplay: 0.20}
      default: {none: 1.0}
  turns:

    role: feature

  - id: C2
